alignment reliable, you MUST repeat at least one line of the existing code VERBATIM

line VERBATIM immediately after the lines you want to change (a trailing anchor). The
plugin finds those repeated lines in the file to position your edit. Anchor lines are
context only — do not change them.

If there is no line after your edit (e.g. the edit is at the end of the file or you are
editing a single line with no following context), just repeat the leading anchor and
the new lines.

You may edit the line at the cursor or nearby lines, and you may add or remove lines.
Do NOT explain your decisions. Do NOT return markdown blocks ```.
The anchor line and your new lines must preserve existing whitespace/indentation.

```python

    return <|CURSOR_IS_HERE|> * height
print(area(3, 4))
```

Desired result:
```python

    return width * height
print(area(3, 4))
```

CORRECT response (repeat the anchor line verbatim, then the new line, then echo the
next line as a trailing anchor):
```python
def area(width, height):
    return width * height
print(area(3, 4))
```

The first line (`def area(width, height):`) is the verbatim anchor the plugin
uses to locate the edit; the second line is the new content; the third line
(`print(area(3, 4))`) is the trailing anchor that tells the plugin where the edit
ends.

## Example: cursor is indented (edit adds lines)

Existing code (cursor on the indented blank line):
```lua
function print_sign(number)
    if number > 0 then
        print("Positive")
    <|CURSOR_IS_HERE|>
    end
end
```

Desired result:
```lua
function print_sign(number)
    if number > 0 then
        print("Positive")
    else
        print("Non‑positive")
    end
end
```

CORRECT response (anchor = the `if` line, verbatim; then the new lines; then echo
the `    end` line as a trailing anchor):
```lua
    if number > 0 then
        print("Positive")
    else
        print("Non‑positive")
    end
```

The anchor (`    if number > 0 then`) is unchanged context. The lines after it are the
edit. The plugin trims the already-present `print("Positive")` line automatically.
The trailing `    end` line tells the plugin where the edit ends.


## Fish Shell

- Use snake_case for names
- Use long options, i.e. `--quiet` over `-q`, `--regex` over `-r`

```fish
function gdX
    # cumulative diff (see my gdlc for just one commit)
    set num (string replace --regex 'gd(ic)?[su]*' '' $argv)
    if string match --quiet --regex 'gdic' $argv # gdic == git diff w/ icdiff
        echo "git-icdiff HEAD~$num..HEAD"
        return
    end

    # show the diff _ACROSS_ X commits back
    # gd5 => git diff HEAD~5..HEAD
    echo -n git
    if string match --quiet --regex u $argv
        # u == unified (not side by side) diff
        echo -n " -c delta.side-by-side=false"
    end
    # unlike gdlc, we don't do this across one commit, but across N
    echo " diff HEAD~$num..HEAD"
end

# allow f before or after number (in case I type gpt1 first, vs if i habituate gptf1 which is long term probably where I will go)
function _abbr_git_push_up_to
    set num (string replace --all --regex '[^\d]' '' "$argv") # strip non numbers
    if string match --quiet --regex f "$argv"
        set --function force \--force
    end
    if test -z "$num"
        set commit_ref ""
    else
        set commit_ref "HEAD~$num"
    end
    # refspec has object:dest_ref
    # TODO also use default remote? or?
    set -l branch (git_current_branch)
    set -l push "git push origin $commit_ref%:$branch $force"
    if test -n "$num"; and set -q force
        echo "$push && git prune-unpushed-reflog refs/remotes/origin/$branch $commit_ref..HEAD"
    else
        echo "$push"
    end
end

abbr --regex 'gdlc[u]?\d+' --function gdlcX _gdlcX
abbr --regex 'gdiclc\d+' --function gdlcX _gdiclcX
function gdlcX
    set num (string replace --regex '^gd(ic)?lc[u]?' '' $argv)
    set prev (math $num - 1)
    if string match --quiet --regex 'gdic' $argv # gdic == git diff w/ icdiff
        echo "git-icdiff HEAD~$num..HEAD~$prev"
        return
    end
    echo -n git
    if string match --quiet --regex u $argv
        # u == unified (not side by side) diff
        echo -n " -c delta.side-by-side=false"
    end
    echo " log --patch HEAD~$num..HEAD~$prev"
end

if status is-interactive
    function pwd --description "pwd for a repository => repo root in yellow + repo dir in white"
        # if this causes grief, go back to just prd
        if not isatty stdout
            builtin pwd $argv
            return
        end
        # PRN support -P/-L arg like builtin does, and set default behavior of not resolving symlinks (-L) because right now the below defaults as if -P was passed (it resolves symlinks)

        if test (builtin pwd) = /
            # at root of fs, don't show // # TODO come back and rework below to drop the trailing / as I don't think I like that differing vs pwd.. especially b/c I do demos with this and the color is fine but less so altering the path even if the same.. NBD but might as well be consistent
            echo -s (set_color normal) /
            return
        end
        _pwd
    end
end

function _pwd

    # FYI test w/ split pane in iterm2 (open lots of example paths, /, ~/, in a github repo, in nested repo dir) => use broadcast Cmd+Shift+I and send Cmd+K => pwd => command pwd  # compare results
    set _rr (_repo_root)

    # prefix w/in repo (beneat repo root), prepend / for join logic below to avoid trailing / in final output (so pwd matches command pwd)
    set _prefix "/"(git rev-parse --show-prefix 2>/dev/null)
    set -l _prefix (string replace -r '/$' '' $_prefix) # strip trailing / from rev-parse (or if in repo root, from prepended / which is also trailing)

    if string match -q -r '(?<host_dir>.*/(bitbucket|github|gitlab))/(?<repo>.*)' $_rr
        # path is normal color thru host dir (i.e. ~/repos/github), then cyan for org/repo, then white for the repo dir(s)
        echo -s (set_color normal) $host_dir / \
            (set_color cyan) $repo \
            (set_color yellow) $_prefix \
            (set_color normal)
    else
        # else path is normal through repo root and white for the repo dir(s)
        echo -s (set_color normal) $_rr \
            (set_color yellow) $_prefix \
            (set_color normal)
    end

    # PRN I like leaving white / on end of path but builtin for pwd doesn't include the final slash, I like it right now b/c it makes it clear that it is the root of a repo
end

function _repo_root # xonsh-value-getter

    # FYI missing git command should break returning a path
    if not command -q git
        echo "[FAIL] git not found" >&2
        return 1
    end

    if git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree 2>/dev/null 1>/dev/null
        git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null
    else if command -q hg && hg root 2>/dev/null 1>/dev/null
        # FYI don't let missing hg command break machines w/o hg repos
        hg root 2>/dev/null
    else
        builtin pwd
    end

end

    if test -n "$(git status --porcelain)"

    git commit -m "Add LICENSE.txt"
```
